newsitem.title: UK: MINOR METALS - Slow, lacks solid consumer interest.
newsitem.headline: MINOR METALS - Slow, lacks solid consumer interest.

text.p: Expected consumer covering for fourth quarter requirements failed to emerge in force during this week's minor metals trading, though traders said the consumers would soon be a driving influence in the market. "Consumers are still generally holding off and are living hand to mouth at present, although they will need to start covering soon," one commented. A bounce in molybdendum and vanadium was noted, but several traders believed the uptick may soon falter. Elsewhere the recent star of the sector, cobalt, held firm in scant trading.
Tight nearby supplies, a shortage of concentrate and merchant short-covering triggered gains in molybdendum.

"Its turned around again...there is talk of a lack of supplies flowing from producer Codelco," one trader said. "Rumour has it Codelco has hit bad ore bodies and are struggling to meet their commitments," another added. THis could not be immediately confirmed. But with fourth quarter requirements likely to be completed soon molybdendum prices could stall and possibily drift back.
Vanadium benefited from a concentrate shortage and low inventoriess. Chinese material was also said in short supply.
"Molybdendum and vanadium have seen some consumer buying, though this could dry up in Novemeber," a European source said.
Cobalt after recent brisk bouts of short-covering maintained firm levels in quiet business. "The pace of enquiry has slowed over the last two weeks," said a trader.
He believed prices would remain firm over the coming months against the backdrop of tight Russian supplies.

Others also saw a price spike, adding cobalt was also deriving some support from a pick-up in U.S. consumer demand. Little in the way of fundamental news emerged in the minor metal sector, though some traders were looking at Zaire's political situation. Zaire is important producer of cobalt.
There has been speculation inside Zaire about President Mobutu's health since prostate surgery in a Swiss hospital on August 22.

The government has shown strong sensitivity to any suggestion Mobutu's illness could be terminal. This week it suspended a newspaper that reported the president was riddled with cancer and was to undergo another operation.
Zaire's Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo Wa Dondo told a news conference in Brussels on Wednesday Mobutu would return home next month, adding that he was recovering well.

"We are not in an after-Mobutu phase and we cannot begin to speculate about it," he declared. Manganese amid the lack of Chinese producer selling eyed higher levels. Traders believed substantial contracts were soon to be completed, with some suggesting near-term levels above $1,500 as realistic levels for manganese metal.

But at an Association of Mining Analysts presentation in London on Thursday, Yves Rambaud, chairman of French metals group Eramet said the longer-term demand outlook for manganese was not particularly bullish.
"Manganese for metallic projects we see as flat to a small growth in consumption, and in chemicals no great growth expectations," he said.

Rambaud added that the steel industry accounts for 90 percent of manganese demand, and the chemical industry 10 percent. Eramet has a 46 percent share in Comilog, a company which operates a large Manganese field in Moanda, Gabon.

Comilog produced 1.016 million wet tons of manganese ore during he first half of 1996 from 986,000 tons in the year-ago period. The company is one of the three top producers in the world, with annual output of around two million wet tons of ore.
Tungsten ferro adopted a downside bent after finding few consumers willing to buy at the lower end of the market. A glut of nearby material was also dampening upside enthusiasm.
Antimony drifted lower as Chinese material remained free flowing. This helped to maintain reasonable stock levels in Europe, traders said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 8075
